body:
`event:india-stagnation-taper-2010-13` | confidence: **verified** | tags: india, policy, base-rate, cyclical, macro

After touching ~21,000 in Nov 2010 the Sensex went sideways-to-down for three years: ~15,100 in Dec 2011 (approximate) and a taper-tantrum low near ~18,000 in Aug 2013, while small caps fell much more (BSE Smallcap roughly -40% in 2011; unverified). Causes: inflation near double digits and 13 RBI rate hikes in 2010-11 (from memory), 'policy paralysis' and corruption scandals (2G, coal), stalled projects that later became bank NPAs, a current-account deficit near ~4.8% of GDP in FY13. On 22 May 2013 the Fed signalled tapering; Indian markets sold off - the Sensex fell 12% in 20 sessions from July, and on 16 Aug 2013 it fell 3.97% (769 points) to 18,598 and the Nifty 4.08% to 5,507.85, the biggest daily fall since 2011. The rupee lost almost 15% between 22 May and 30 Aug 2013, hitting a record ~68.8/USD on 28 Aug 2013 (from memory; sources found cite 62-64 mid-August). RBI tightened abruptly; Raghuram Rajan took over in Sept 2013 and the FCNR(B) deposit swap rebuilt reserves. Leaders: IT, pharma, FMCG (dollar earners, defensives); laggards: infra, PSU banks, realty, capital goods. Bottom signals: rupee capitulation plus forceful policy response, maximum pessimism, mid/small caps at multi-year low valuations (P/B near ~1 for many). Lesson: currency crises mark bottoms when policy credibly responds.

data.section: Backtest: US insider-buying clusters (Form 4, code P) — small/mid caps, signals 2021–2024

title: insider_clusters_us › Backtest: US insider-buying clusters (Form 4, code P) — small/mid caps, signals 2021–2024

body:
1. **Survivorship.** 221 of ~1,180 otherwise-eligible events (~19%) had no Yahoo history. SEC audit of the
   189 non-biotech ones: **162 were acquired** (merger proxy/tender filed after the event), **23 went bankrupt**
   (8-K item 1.03), 4 deregistered. None of the usable series ended mid-window (Yahoo simply drops delisted
   tickers), so the usable sample is survivors-only. Controls have the same bias (29% of the random pool missing).
2. **Bound.** If every missing acquired event earned +25% excess and every bankrupt −80% inside the window,
   the blended 12m excess would rise from 0.0% to about **+2.1%** — still small, and an upper-ish bound because
   controls also lose their acquired firms and many takeovers came > 12 months after the signal.
3. **Overlap / dependence.** Events cluster in time (e.g. 2022 sell-off, Mar-2023 bank stress). Month-clustered
   bootstrap handles part of this; it is not a full calendar-time factor regression (no FF5/momentum alpha here).
4. **Market cap** from cover-page shares × insider price; multi-class issuers understated; 669 events had no
   frame and were dropped (skews to larger, XBRL-compliant filers).
5. **Control draw sensitivity.** Re-running with a slightly different event set moved control-relative means by
   ~0.5–1 pp (e.g. 3m −1.6% → −1.0%) — noise level, conclusions unchanged.
6. **Window.** Four signal years, one regime. A null here is not proof the effect never exists; it is evidence
   the plain public rule was not worth paying for in this period.
7. **Costs** ignored (would make results worse, especially for $300M–$1B names).
8. Code P also includes privately negotiated purchases; the 180-day listing filter removes most IPO/PIPE cases
   but not all.
title: insider_clusters_us › 5. Caveats (read before using any number)

body:
Keep the v2 structure (judgment fraud signals hard at entry; auditor exit and accounting-trouble events hard at exit;
cash-flow tests as questions; P/E in stage 5). Changes from v2:
- **Pledge becomes the top graded red flag, with numbers:** > 50% of promoter holding = graded red at "strong"
  level (needs a written override: why the pledge exists, the lender, the margin-call price vs today's price); > 25% =
  graded red (normal override). Rising pledge (≥ 10 pp in a year) = escalation, untested beyond 13 cases. Still
  **not hard** (Alok, Jindal Stainless, Zen Technologies).
- **Pledge + interest cover < 1.5x together** = the main stage-2 "look much harder, size small" combination
  (post-hoc, so it needs a forward check).
- **Confirmed questions, not flags:** CFO/PAT, debt growth with negative CFO, other-income share, debtor-day jumps —
  ask what working capital is made of and who owes the money.
- **No mechanical "any flag" gate:** it would have cut 47% of later ≥ 3x winners.
- Proof still missing for the judgment rules (H1a–H5) — they cannot be tested mechanically; the forward scoreboard
  (stage 7) is where they get tested.

data.section: Recommendation (new record insight:disqualifiers-v3-proposal; v2 and insight:disqualifiers unchanged)

title: hard_filters_india_v2 › Recommendation (new record insight:disqualifiers-v3-proposal; v2 and insight:disqualifiers unchanged)

body:
- **Pledge.** Promoter pledged/encumbered shares ÷ promoter shares, from BSE shareholding-pattern XBRL, parsed with
  `hard_filters_v2/h2_panel.pledge_from` (unchanged). BSE code from the firm's screener page (else none ⇒ unknown).
  **Budget deviation, fixed now:** fetching the latest SHP before every one of ~10,000 events would take ~10,000 BSE
  requests (~5 h at one stream ≥ 1.6 s). Instead, for each firm we fetch its SHP list plus **one SHP per calendar
  year: the June-quarter SHP** (2017–2025). An event uses the **latest of these fetched June-quarter SHPs whose BSE
  filing date is before the event date**, and only if that quarter ended ≤ 15 months before the event. Staleness is
  therefore 0–15 months (mean ≈ 7). Stated bias: stale pledge readings misclassify some flagged firms as unflagged
  and vice versa — this dilutes group differences, i.e. it works *against* H1/H2. `B25` = pledge > 25%, `B50` = > 50%.
  A SHP declaring no promoter pledge = 0%; no promoter shares = 0%; no XBRL / parse failure = unknown.
- **Annual flags.** Screener **standalone** company page (cached from `bt_solv_in/sc/` or `bt_pead_surv/sc/`, else
  fetched) and its *Cash from Financing Activity* schedule (needed for S4's dividends). Annual columns are cut with
  `solvency_india/s3_panel.cut` at **FY0 = the latest fiscal-year column ending ≤ event date − 6 months** (annual
  reports are due within ~6 months; same convention as the solvency test's T − 6 months) and with a balance sheet at
  the same date; then `solvency_screen.inputs()` / `flags()` unchanged. **S2** = interest cover (EBIT / interest)
  < 1.5x; **S5-India** = ≥ 2 of S1 (negative net worth, not payout-driven), S2, S4 (dividends > FCF while borrowings
  rose). FY0 more than 24 months before the event ⇒ unknown (firm stopped filing). Stated biases: restated, not
  as-first-reported screener numbers; standalone accounts under-flag holdco debt. Financials are **not** excluded
  from the event set (they are in it); for them S2/S5 usually come out unknown or not meaningful — reported as a
  sensitivity (financials excluded).
- **RED** (any red flag) = B25 ∨ S2 ∨ S5-India. RED = 1 if any known component fires; RED = 0 only if pledge is known
  **and** S2 is known and none of the known components fires (S5 may be unknown — it needs S4); otherwise unknown and
  the event is excluded from groups A–D (counted). Sensitivity: unknown treated as RED = 0.
